run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T22:06:04Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by real error spans on that service: 427 error ingress spans (HTTP 500/503/504) and 393 error router-egress spans in the 84-minute window, with the 5-minute ingress error rate rising from ~0.004-0.015/s after 21:50 to a peak of ~1.04/s at 22:13-22:14 and back to ~0.015/s by 22:21. Two trace-verified failure modes reach frontend-proxy through the frontend service: (a) at ~22:07:55, frontend GET /api/data returned 500 because its grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds call failed with gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE ('No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080'), which is the ad Service ClusterIP; (b) at ~22:14:45, a load-generator GET got 504 after 15.3 s because frontend's /api/data took 24.6 s, of which ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds took 22.4 s waiting on flagd ResolveBoolean calls that ended in DEADLINE_EXCEEDED. The deepest measured mechanism under the ad slowness is CPU contention inside the ad pod: Deployment ad was rolled out at 22:07:24Z (restartedAt annotation, new ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5, old pod killed), and the new pod ran at 95-100% CFS throttling against a 50m CPU limit from 22:09 to 22:17 (old pod 8-32%), consuming its full 0.05-core cap, while flagd itself used ~0.003 cores with 0% throttling. The flagd-config ConfigMap holds one switched-on fault-injection flag, adFailure = "on" ("Fail ad service"), which names the failing workload; that is the leading root-cause candidate, but its causal link and switch-on time could not be verified, and the parallel 503 mode (frontend-proxy -> frontend connect failures from 21:48) has no established cause. Conclusion is partial.

claims.text: frontend-proxy emitted 427 STATUS_CODE_ERROR ingress spans (HTTP 504/503/500) and 393 STATUS_CODE_ERROR 'router frontend egress' spans over the 84-minute window, so the alerting service itself has error evidence.

frontend-proxy 'ingress' error rate at 60 s resolution: 0 at 21:46-21:49, 0.0037-0.0148/s from 21:50 to 22:08, 0.211 at 22:09:04, peak 1.037 at 22:13:04, then 0.015-0.021/s from 22:21 onward; the alert anchored at 22:06:04 falls in the low-level (0.0148/s) phase.

The frontend service has its own error evidence: 393 error spans on 'GET /api/data', 393 error spans on 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' (of 1888 calls in the window) and 15.2 error 'tcp.connect' spans; its error rate was 0 until 22:08:04, 0.33-1.12/s from 22:09 to 22:19, and 0 from 22:21.

One full trace shows the timeout chain: load-generator GET 15.31 s HTTP 504 <- frontend-proxy ingress 15.00 s HTTP 504 <- frontend 'GET /api/data' 24.59 s <- frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' 24.59 s <- ad 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' 22.37 s, whose three 'resolve' child spans took 2.0 s, 3.6 s and 2.3 s and whose ad-side 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean' client spans carry rpc.grpc.status_code=4 with the flagd span logging 'context deadline exceeded'.

At ~22:07:55 frontend 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' spans returned HTTP 500 with exception.message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080', their grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds child spans carried rpc.grpc.status_code=14, and frontend-proxy ingress repeated the HTTP 500; 100.70.197.56:8080 is the ad Service ClusterIP and port.

A second, earlier failure mode exists: frontend-proxy ingress returned HTTP 503 with a 'router frontend egress' child of status error=true, http.status_code=0 and no frontend span at all, e.g. at 21:48:34, 21:51:14, 21:54:53, 22:01:xx, 22:04:42 and 22:04:59, which indicates the proxy never obtained a response from the frontend.

Deployment ad was rolled out at 22:07:24Z: its pod template carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T22:07:24Z, and the events show 'Scaled up replica set ad-785b4464f5 from 0 to 1', 'Scaled down replica set ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0', 'Deleted pod: ad-554b849958-w5fhc' and a new pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh scheduled/created/started at 22:07:25-22:07:26 (restart count 0).
The ad container is capped at cpu limit 50m (request 10m) and memory limit 450Mi, and has no readiness, liveness or startup probe.

CFS throttling ratio for the new ad pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh was 0.954 at 22:09:04, 0.981 at 22:11:04, 0.996 at 22:13:04, 1.0 at 22:15:04, 0.880 at 22:17:04, 0.641 at 22:21:04 and 0.26-0.35 afterwards, versus 0.08-0.32 for the replaced pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc and 0 for the flagd container throughout.

ad container CPU usage rose from 0.005-0.008 cores on the old pod to 0.0157-0.0493 cores on the new pod between 22:09 and 22:19 (i.e. at its 0.05-core limit), while flagd used only ~0.0028-0.0048 cores over the same interval.

The otel-demo ConfigMap flagd-config contains key demo.flagd.json with the fault-injection flag adFailure defaultVariant "on" (description 'Fail ad service', state ENABLED), while every other flag there (adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, paymentFailure, productCatalogFailure, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, emailMemoryLeak, paymentUnreachable, recommendationCacheFailure) has defaultVariant "off".

ad itself recorded no error status on its server side: 1495 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' spans with STATUS_CODE_UNSET and no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series, 1278 getAdsByCategory and 443 getRandomAds spans, with only a periodic 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' error series (1.02 over the window); its ad-pod logs from 22:17:46-22:18:14 show normal 'Targeted ad request received' / 'Non-targeted ad request received' lines and no error/fail/deadline line among the 340 lines read.
Node pod-CPU totals were stable at ~0.45-0.56 cores on node i-040b429451d033123 and rose from ~0.05 to ~0.20 cores on node i-0038dc80421276490 at 22:17-22:21.

fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-zzt65 container 'fraud-detection' was OOMKilled with exitCode 137 at 2026-11-17T21:42:02Z (restartCount 1, memory limit 400Mi) and its throttling ratio rose to 0.699-0.840 at 22:15-22:21, while frontend throttling stayed flat at ~0.27-0.32 for the whole window.

The declared fault mode of adFailure ('Fail ad service') is not what was observed on ad: ad's own GetAds server spans carry no ERROR status and ad logs show successful serving, so the failure surfaced as latency and connection failure, not as ad-returned errors; additionally ad's own flagd resolutions were timing out, so whether ad evaluated adFailure as on cannot be shown from the telemetry.

flagd itself shows no resource problem: its container used ~0.0028 cores with 0 CFS throttling and the flagd pod had 0 restarts and was ready, so the ad-side 'context deadline exceeded'/'deadline exceeded' resolutions are not explained by flagd CPU exhaustion.

frontend CPU throttling (~0.27-0.32 of periods, pod restart count 0) is flat across the whole window and does not change at the 22:09 error onset, so frontend CPU quota exhaustion does not coincide with the error burst.

fraud-detection's OOMKill (exit 137 at 21:42:02) and its 22:14 container recreations are not the cause of the frontend-proxy request errors: it is a different workload with its own container failure, it precedes the 21:50 error onset, and no traced call path ties its failures to frontend or frontend-proxy error responses; its 22:15-22:21 throttling spike only coincides in time.

A flagd pod failure or flagd restart during the incident window is not supported: the flagd pod was created at 21:37:10Z with restartCount 0 for both containers and 0% CPU throttling for the whole window, so flagd unavailability was not observed.

Leading candidate root cause: ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config, whose adFailure flag is switched on ('on', 'Fail ad service', state ENABLED) and names the workload that is failing; no other object was seen applying a fault to the ad service, and the ad deployment restart at 22:07:24Z (restartedAt annotation, new ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5) is consistent with a restart made in response to ad failing. The switch-on time and the exact behavioural link remain unproven.

Mechanism candidate: after the 22:07:24Z rollout the ad pod's 50m CPU quota became the binding constraint (95-100% CFS throttling, usage pinned at 0.05 cores), so each ad GetAds spent tens of seconds including 2-3.6 s flagd resolutions, frontend /api/data exceeded the 15 s proxy deadline, and frontend-proxy emitted 504s; this matches the 22:09-22:20 error burst and its subsidence as throttling fell to 0.64 and then 0.26-0.35.

Second candidate, unresolved: the 503 errors from frontend-proxy to the frontend (router egress status 0, no frontend span, both 26 ms and 615 ms durations, from 21:48 through 22:04) point to the frontend not answering/accepting the proxy's upstream connections; the frontend container has no readiness probe, was ready with 0 restarts and is now the only ready endpoint, so the historical cause cannot be pinned from the available telemetry.

Have an operator check the current value and recent history of demo.flagd.json flag adFailure in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config and, if it is not intentionally injected, set it to off, then compare ad GetAds latency and frontend-proxy error rate before drawing the causal conclusion.

Review the ad container's cpu limit of 50m against its post-restart demand (usage pinned at its 0.05-core cap with 95-100% CFS throttling) and add a readiness probe so a starting or saturated ad pod is not immediately placed in the Service endpoints.

gaps: Change history is not integrated in this Run, so when adFailure in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config was set to "on" and who applied kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T22:07:24Z to Deployment ad are unknown.

The declared fault itself (ad returning failures because of adFailure=on) was not observed: ad's GetAds spans carry no error status and its logs show normal serving, and ad's own flagd resolutions were timing out, so the flag-value-to-symptom link is unverified.

The alert rule definition could not be read: list_prometheus_rules for rule name RequestErrorRate returned no_data (b146254b-0871-463e-b6bc-a52cb8e61f9d-t0:4782e492-c5dc-479e-81ad-e219782d272d), so the exact expression and threshold behind 'current: 2.4555' are unknown.

The flagd container produced no readable log lines (0 bytes read for containers flagd, flagd-ui and init-config; a0e22de4-a4aa-445d-a537-3251f41f8ae7-t1:0e34eaa2-f2ea-42bc-bacd-9a6b99de8236 is no_data), so flagd's server-side view of the 2-3.6 s ResolveBoolean deadlines could not be checked.

The frontend container produced no readable log lines and the filtered query returned no_data (9d02f0a5-e2e1-4f74-9e7f-bdc654f4a57e-t1:fba4b15e-fe92-46b5-abbc-6af5f302c55e), so frontend-side application errors behind the 503 responses could not be inspected.

The cause of the 503 frontend-proxy -> frontend connect failures between 21:48 and 22:07 is not established; there is no readiness probe whose failures could be observed, no event was recorded for the frontend pod, and pod/endpoint state is available only as of query time (22:30-22:32), not during that interval.

rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count returned no series for any service in this window (665ff083-0ad8-4f07-9b9e-1f92684af16c-t0:fbd16a39-e620-4f23-8c20-8b572334ea74 is no_data), so RPC latency histograms could not be used to corroborate the span-duration observations.

The ad-service span-metric series for its flagd ResolveBoolean calls reported 0 calls and 0 errors over the window although error spans for those calls appear in traces, so metric-based counting of that specific call path is unreliable.

No node-level CPU allocatable, pressure-condition or throttling metric was available (kube_node.* and rpc_/http_ metric name queries returned no_data; only container_* series and their node totals exist), so whether node saturation contributed to the ad pod's throttling cannot be assessed.

The ad pod's current logs were read from 22:17:46-22:18:14 only (the newest 40 of 340 lines shown, and the container has no previous instance), so ad behaviour during the 21:50-22:10 failure onset was not directly inspected.
fraud-detection's 70-84% throttling at 22:15-22:21 and its 22:14 container recreations were not tied to this cause and remain an unexplained change during the window.
next_steps: Confirm with the cluster owner whether the adFailure flag in otel-demo/flagd-config was intentionally enabled and when, and whether the 22:07:24Z restart of Deployment ad was the corresponding remediation attempt.
Capture the Deployment ad restart history and flagd-config revision history from the change/audit system, which this investigation could not query.
If the 503 mode recurs, record frontend pod events and probe/endpoint state at that time, and consider adding readiness probes so proxy upstream failures can be attributed.
Re-check ad GetAds latency and frontend-proxy 5xx rate after adFailure is returned to off and ad CPU limits are reviewed, to confirm or reject the causal chain.
